pool.sol:
\( \text{The dot product of two vectors } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} c \\ d \end{pmatrix} \text{ is given by } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = ac + bd. \)

\( \text{In this case, } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}. \)

\( \text{Therefore, } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = (3)(-4) + (4)(3) = -12 + 12 = 0. \)

\( \text{A dot product of 0 indicates that the vectors are orthogonal.} \)

pool.text: Consider the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \). Let \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \). This is equivalent to finding the projection of \( \mathbf{b} \) onto the column space of \( A \), denoted by \( \text{Col}(A) \). The normal equations for this least squares problem are \( A^T A \mathbf{x} = A^T \mathbf{b} \). This set of vectors is already orthogonal since \( \mathbf{c}_1 \cdot \mathbf{c}_2 = (1)(1) + (1)(-1) = 0 \). Thus, \( \{\mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2\} = \{\mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2\} \) is an orthogonal basis. The problem asks to find the projection of \( \mathbf{v} \) onto the subspace spanned by \( \mathbf{a}_1 \) and \( \mathbf{a}_2 \), which is the entire \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) in this case, as \( \{\mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2\} \) forms a basis for \( \mathbb{R}^2 \).
